title: Uniform adic lifting from a power-split completed algebra in a fixed graded target class
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $r\geq0$, and $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and suppose $B=P/J$ is $I$-adically complete. Let $\delta:J/J^2\to B^{\oplus r}$ be the $B$-linear map $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, with derivatives extended continuously from polynomials. Suppose $c\geq0$ and for every $a\in I^c$ there is a $B$-linear $h_a:B^{\oplus r}\to J/J^2$ satisfying $h_a\delta=a\operatorname{id}_{J/J^2}$. Fix a Noetherian $I$-adically complete commutative $A$-algebra $C_0$. For any $A$-algebra $D$, write $I^nD$ for the ideal generated by images of elements of $I^n$ and put $\operatorname{gr}_I(D)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^nD/I^{n+1}D$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], with multiplication of homogeneous representatives induced by multiplication in $D$ and the degree-zero map from $A/I$. Then there exist integers $e\geq0$ and $n_0\geq e+1$ such that for every Noetherian $I$-adically complete commutative $A$-algebra $C$ admitting a degree-preserving $A/I$-algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{gr}_I(C)\cong\operatorname{gr}_I(C_0)$, every $n\geq n_0$, and every $A$-algebra homomorphism $\psi:B\to C/I^nC$, there is an $A$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:B\to C$ such that the composites of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ to $C/I^{n-e}C$ agree.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), using the conormal formulation of Tag 0GAJ (lemma-equivalent-with-artin-smooth), condition (3). Uniformity over the graded target class follows from the definitions d(S), q(S) in local-cohomology.tex, Tag 0GA6 (section-uniform).

proof.text: The finite type algebra $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Thus $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_t)$ is finitely generated, and the classes of the $f_j$ generate $J/J^2$ over $B$: any coefficient in $P$ acts through its residue in $B$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-graded-power-split-linear-factorization] once with $(R_0,K_0,c)=(C_0,IC_0,c)$; denote its constants by $e,N$ and set $n_0=N\geq2e+1$. For any permitted $C$, put $K=IC$. The ideals $K^j$ equal $I^jC$: both are generated by products of $j$ images of elements of $I$. Hence the graded isomorphism in the item is a degree-preserving unital ring isomorphism of the kind the linear lemma requires. These same $e,N$ work for all such $C$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text: Fix $m\geq N$ and an $A$-algebra map $\psi_m:B\to C/K^m$, and put $R_m=C/K^m$. Choose lifts $y_i\in C$ of $\psi_m(x_i)$. The evaluation lemma [lem-per-completed-polynomial-taylor-evaluation], also applied to the complete algebra $R_m$, shows that $F=E_y:P\to C$ reduces to $\psi_m$ after $P\to B$: both maps out of $P$ have the same coordinates. Consequently $F(J)\subseteq K^m$ and $F(J^2)\subseteq K^{2m}$. Set $M=(J/J^2)\otimes_B R_m$ and let $d:M\to R_m^{\oplus r}$ be the scalar extension of $\delta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This is a finite module: it is generated by the finitely many $\bar f_j\otimes1$. The formula $u(\bar g\otimes b)=bF(g)\bmod K^{2m}$ defines an $R_m$-linear map $M\to K^m/K^{2m}$. Indeed changing $g$ by $J^2$ changes $F(g)$ by $K^{2m}$, and changing a lift of a scalar in $R_m$ changes the product by $K^mK^m$. The $B$-balancing identity follows because $F(p)\bmod K^m=\psi_m(\bar p)$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text: The maps $h_a$ in the hypothesis tensor with $R_m$ to give $h_a^{(m)}d=\psi_m(a)\operatorname{id}_M$. Every $b\in K^c=I^cC$ is a finite sum $b=\sum_jt_ja_j$ with $t_j\in C$ and $a_j$ images of elements of $I^c$. Thus $\sum_j\bar t_jh_{a_j}^{(m)}$ factors multiplication by $\bar b$ through $d$. These are precisely the power-splitting hypotheses of [lem-per-graded-power-split-linear-factorization]. With $s=m-e$, that lemma gives $v:R_m^{\oplus r}\to K^s/K^{2s}$ satisfying $vd=\rho u$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text:
Choose $t_i\in K^s$ representing $v$ of the $i$th standard basis vector, and put $F'=E_{y-t}$. Since $m\geq N\geq2e+1$, we have $s\geq1$ and $2s>m$. The Taylor congruence [lem-per-completed-polynomial-taylor-evaluation] gives, for every $g\in J$,
$$F'(g)\equiv F(g)-\sum_i F(\partial_i g)t_i\equiv (\rho u)(\bar g\otimes1)-(vd)(\bar g\otimes1)=0\pmod {K^{2s}}.$$
Here $d(\bar g\otimes1)$ has coordinates $F(\partial_i g)\bmod K^m$; a change of representative changes the product by $K^{m+s}\subseteq K^{2s}$. Thus $F'$ factors through a map $\psi_{2s}':B\to C/K^{2s}$. The first congruence of the evaluation lemma shows that it agrees with $\psi_m$ modulo $K^s$. This proves the one-step improvement at every $m\geq N$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text: Starting with $m_0=n$ and $\psi^0=\psi$, repeat step 5: set $m_{i+1}=2(m_i-e)$ and choose $\psi^{i+1}:B\to C/K^{m_{i+1}}$ agreeing with $\psi^i$ modulo $K^{s_i}$, where $s_i=m_i-e$. Inductively $m_i=2e+2^i(n-2e)$, so $m_i\geq N$, $s_i$ is strictly increasing, and $s_i\to\infty$. Put $\eta_i=\psi^i\bmod K^{s_i}$. Then $\eta_{i+1}\bmod K^{s_i}=\eta_i$, by the congruence just proved and $s_{i+1}\leq m_{i+1}$. Repeated reduction gives compatibility at any two indices. For each $q\geq1$, reduce any $\eta_i$ with $s_i\geq q$ to obtain a map $\theta_q:B\to C/K^q$ independent of $i$. These maps are compatible for all $q$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

proof.text: By $K$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], the map $C\to\varprojlim_q C/K^q$ is bijective. For $b\in B$ define $\varphi(b)$ to be the unique element with residues $\theta_q(b)$. Componentwise operations and injectivity of this map give $\varphi(b+b')=\varphi(b)+\varphi(b')$, $\varphi(bb')=\varphi(b)\varphi(b')$, $\varphi(1)=1$, and the $A$-scalar identity, since each $\theta_q$ is an $A$-algebra map. At $q=s_0=n-e$ the residue is $\eta_0=\psi\bmod K^{n-e}$. This is the required map and the required agreement. The bound $n_0=N\geq2e+1$ in particular implies $n_0\geq e+1$.

source.place: Tag 0GAQ (lemma-get-morphism-general-better), proof, with remark-improve-homomorphism and Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NX-aacbe2a47 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and both new nodes in full against restricted.tex 0GAJ(3), 0AK3, remark-improve-homomorphism and 0GAQ (with its proof), local-cohomology.tex 0GA6 (d(S), q(S) depend only on gr), the (A,n,c)-module definition, 0GAC (with its proof) and 0GAD, more-algebra lemma-near-projective, and formal-spaces remark-universal-property and remark-I-adic-completion-and-restricted-power-series. The item statement is unchanged. Step by step: step 1 gets J finitely generated from Hilbert basis and Noetherian completion. Step 2 uses (IC)^j=I^jC, so the A/I-algebra graded isomorphism is a ring isomorphism, and n0=N>=2e+1. Step 3 applies Taylor uniqueness on R_m=C/K^m, which is complete because K is nilpotent there; any A-algebra map out of P is continuous, so F mod K^m = psi_m composed with P->B, and the error map u is well defined and B-balanced. Step 4 extends the splittings to b=sum t_j a_j in I^cC, which gives a near-projective (R,n,c)-module. Step 5 is the second Taylor congruence together with vd=rho u; the representative change lies in K^(m+s), contained in K^(2s), and s>=1 with 2s>m. Steps 6 and 7 check out: m_i=2e+2^i(n-2e), the reductions eta_i are compatible, and the limit exists by bijectivity of C to its completion. Linear lemma: e=(d+2)c and N=max(q+e,2e+1) meet every threshold of 0GAC (n>=q+(1+d)c, n>=(2+d)c, n>=q+2c when d=0, n>=c). Setting v = sum of red∘psi_j∘h_{a_j} gives vd=rho u. It needs only 0GAC, so it avoids the 0GAD Ext_{A/I^c} typo, which is correctly reported as a source error. Taylor node: true for finitely generated I by 05GG (I^mP is the kernel to A[x]/I^m), splitting f into a polynomial plus an I^(2s)P part; I tested r=0, coordinates y not in IT, and characteristic 2 with x^2. Neither new node restates the item. Duplicate search with rg -L over dag/nodes (0GAC, 0GAD, 0AK3, 0AJM, 0GAQ, Taylor, restricted power series, unique continuous homomorphism) found no duplicate; lem-per-formal-monoid-adic-evaluation is adic in the variables too and requires coordinates in the ideal. B1-B3 and B9 hold, and the searches are of three kinds. I accept the declared tool uses: lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian is a Mathlib leaf, and lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian is a generic black box. No SGA is used.
